- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is mixed or neutral; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecasts >+10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00s), model tends to overfit short-term momentum; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day after day 5.
